answer: A sponsor vouches for each newcomer, locking a 60-credit bond and paying a fee: the kth vouch costs k squared credits, so the first costs 1, the tenth 100, and the hundredth 10,000. Minting 1,000 fakes through one sponsor costs 333,833,500 credits in fees plus 60,000 locked bonds, while an honest sponsor pays 1 credit once. Auditors check the ridge register: each vouch ties to one ridge trail record and one walnut cache tended on the tundra route for one epoch. A reused record or untended cache burns the bond. A rented-sponsor ring fails because fees follow the sponsor, not the wallet.
